account: It is six in the morning on day 1; I have just slept at home, so I have not yet seen what anyone is doing today. Yesterday there were several hints of preparations or coordinated supplies. My neighbour said Townsfolk 02 had reported lights or decorations at the bakery, but neither my neighbour nor I confirmed that, and the neighbour said the baker knew of no special occasion. The neighbour also heard the builder asking to meet privately with the innkeeper. Later I personally heard the innkeeper invite the builder to the inn for a private supplies discussion. The secretary reported that Freight was seeking the miller and builder to coordinate warehouse supplies, and passed on hearsay that the baker had carried a sack of bread near the plaza. I also saw Freight carrying a bread sack near town hall. These could be ordinary business, but together they suggest possible preparations involving bread, grain, building supplies, or a gathering. I do not know whether the reports are connected, and have no evidence of danger or wrongdoing. The innkeeper has arranged a confirmed meeting with me today at eighteen hundred in the great hall, ostensibly about the inn's business, and says I need prepare nothing. It might explain some of this, but I cannot assume it will. The town accounts were also missing from the four great hall tables when the secretary searched; I do not know why or whether that is related. Today I should read the appointment book in the morning and keep my scheduled business, including the ten o'clock mill inspection, while asking trustworthy people for firsthand information rather than treating rumours as facts.
